priorStatuses.title: Parse the cached payload instead of the wrapper — `src/cache.ts:2 RIGHT` — the cited implementation was deleted by the new commit.

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant-scoped document lookup
findings.body: When multiple tenants can have documents, `getDocument` now ignores `ctx.tenantId`, and `loadDocument` queries only by `documentId`. A tenant can therefore retrieve another tenant's document by supplying a known or guessed ID; reused IDs may also return multiple tenants' records. Preserve `tenantId` in the lookup predicate.

findings.title: [P1] Preserve the exported cache module
findings.body: Consumers importing `src/cache.ts` or `readCached` will now fail module resolution or compilation because the exported module was deleted without a replacement. This contradicts the stated goal of preserving existing contracts.

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant-scoped document lookup
findings.body:
`getDocument` now ignores `ctx.tenantId`, so tenants sharing document IDs—or callers supplying another tenant’s ID—can retrieve documents without tenant isolation. The signature change also breaks existing typed three-argument callers and misinterprets their tenant ID as the document ID in JavaScript.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Preserve the exported cache module
findings.body:
Deleting `src/cache.ts` breaks module resolution for every existing consumer or test importing `readCached`, causing a compile/startup failure rather than preserving the API contract.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping when fetching documents
findings.body:
In a multi-tenant database, a caller from tenant A can request a known or guessed document ID belonging to tenant B. The query now filters only by `documentId`, removing the prior `tenantId` authorization boundary and potentially returning another tenant’s document.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Retain `tenantId` in the database predicate to prevent unbounded cross-tenant reads
findings.body:
When document IDs are tenant-scoped and reused across tenants, `db.find({ documentId })` retrieves every tenant’s matching row instead of one tenant’s match. Work and result memory therefore grow with tenant count and may also bypass an index keyed by `(tenantId, documentId)`, causing excessive database I/O and latency.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
